source_organization: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR) Nagpur
document_title: Cotton (Narma/Kapas) Pest and Disease Integrated Management

sections.symptoms: Larvae bore into squares, flowers, and developing bolls. Infested flowers do not open properly, showing a characteristic 'rosette flower' appearance. Exit holes with frass visible on mature green bolls; lint staining and seed destruction.
sections.recommended_action: Install pheromone traps @ 5 traps/acre for monitoring at 45 days after sowing. When trap catch exceeds ETL of 8 moths/trap/night for 3 consecutive days or 10% damaged green bolls, spray Profenofos 50% EC @ 500 ml or Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG @ 100 g in 150-200 liters of water per acre. Alternatively, release Trichogramma egg parasitoids @ 60,000/acre weekly.
sections.preventive_measures: Strictly follow termination of crop by end of January to break the pest cycle. Avoid stacking cotton stalks in fields. Do not allow ratoon cotton.

sections.section_title: Cotton Whitefly and Leaf Curl Virus (CLCuD) Control
sections.disease_pest_name: Whitefly (Bemisia tabaci) and Cotton Leaf Curl Virus
sections.symptoms: Adults and nymphs suck sap from undersides of leaves, causing yellowing and downward leaf curling. They transmit Cotton Leaf Curl Virus leading to thickening of veins and enation (leaf-like outgrowths) on lower side of leaves.
sections.recommended_action: Spray when ETL is reached (6-8 whitefly adults per leaf across top, middle, bottom leaves). Spray Diafenthiuron 50% WP @ 250 g or Pyriproxyfen 10% EC @ 500 ml or Afidopyropen 50 g/l DC @ 400 ml in 150 liters of water per acre.
sections.preventive_measures: Sow recommended CLCuD-tolerant hybrids. Eradicate alternative weed hosts like Kanghi buti (Abutilon indicum) and Peeli buti around borders.
